hints.title: Count Excellent Students
hints.text: Count students in each university who achieved scores at or above ninety.

hints.title: Independent Aggregation
hints.text: Compute the qualifying student count for both universities in separate subqueries or common table expressions.

hints.title: Conditional Decision Output
hints.text: Compare the two counts and output the winning institution name or tie indicator.

hints.title: Complete Query
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM NewYork WHERE score >= 90) >
             (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM California WHERE score >= 90)
            THEN 'New York University'
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM NewYork WHERE score >= 90) <
             (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM California WHERE score >= 90)
            THEN 'California University'
        ELSE 'No Winner'
    END AS winner;
```

complexity.time: O(N + C) scanning student scores in both universities
complexity.space: O(1) scalar count aggregation and comparison
complexity.notes: Counts students with scores >= 90 from each table and compares values in CASE.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full cross joins without pre-aggregation create redundant rows.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting independently in subqueries produces scalar values for instant comparison.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle tied counts and output "No Winner".
